hardware.isolation: HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0; GPU1 (RX 7900 XTX) in use by the capacity campaign and not touched

workload.prompt_source: DMS data-manifest validation stream (identical token slice across arms)
workload.route_shape: one resident C1 session per arm, bulk prefill, greedy per-step decode

finding: At 16,384 prompt tokens on the W7900, DMS is slower than dense KV in both flavors while prefill is roughly flat: dense BF16 decodes at 45.98 ms/step, DMS BF16 at 55.39 ms/step (+20.5%), DMS INT8 at 95.48 ms/step (+107.6%, 2.08x dense). Prefill: 623.7 / 616.2 / 608.1 tok/s (-1.2% / -2.5%). The DMS compact payload at this context runs an actual compression ratio of 1.33, and the compact-path gather/scale machinery costs more per decode step than the dense fused attention it replaces at this size. DMS's value on this model is capacity (fitting more retained tokens in limited VRAM, the 24 GB XTX case), not decode speed at moderate context on a 48 GB card.
caveats: Single session, one prompt, one process per arm; diagnostics only - not a retained benchmark and no performance claim.
DMS INT8 is an offline-evaluation codec; it changes attention numerics by design and its decode cost includes INT8 dequant.

16K context with an 8192-token live window: the dense arm attends over the full history; the DMS arms attend over the live window plus compact history through the compact kernel. Longer contexts shift the balance toward DMS as dense attention grows linearly.
